rows.source_contract_text:
The relational corpus remains the source/extraction authority for this experiment.

Relevant current surfaces include:

- `lib/ithkuil/_data/csv/morphemes_atomic.csv`
- `lib/ithkuil/_data/csv/morpheme_compositions.csv`
- `lib/ithkuil/_data/csv/composition_components.csv`
- `lib/ithkuil/_data/csv/source_assertions.csv`
- `lib/ithkuil/_data/csv/grammatical_categories.csv`
- `lib/ithkuil/_data/csv/affix_degrees.csv`
- `lib/ithkuil/_data/csv/root_senses.csv`
- `lib/ithkuil/_data/csv/lexicon_roots.csv`
- `lib/ithkuil/_data/csv/lexicon_root_senses.csv`
- `lib/ithkuil/_data/csv/allomorph_rules.csv`
- `lib/ithkuil/_data/csv/bilqis_ithkuil_crosswalk.csv`
- `lib/ithkuil/_data/csv/bilqis_semantic_bridges.csv`

The existing extraction path is also already substantially deterministic:

- `lib/ithkuil/src/fetch_sources.py`
- `lib/ithkuil/src/build_structure.py`
- `lib/ithkuil/src/build_curriculum_enrichment.py`
- `lib/ithkuil/src/build_morphology.py`
- `lib/ithkuil/src/build_lexicon_chapters.py`
- `lib/ithkuil/src/validate_dataset.py`

The semantic graph **must not** silently replace those source artifacts or reinterpret their evidence status.

The target layering is:

```text
official New Ithkuil grammar + lexicon + affix sources
        |
        v
pinned source snapshots
        |
        v
deterministic source parsers
        |
        v
relational CSV source graph / compiler IR
        |
        v
deterministic SKOS/RDF semantic projection
        |
        +------> JSON-LD / RDF interchange
        |
        +------> FalkorDB materialization
        |
        +------> SPARQL-capable RDF tooling
        |
        +------> SHACL validation when warranted
        |
        +------> OWL entailment when warranted
```

The CSV layer is therefore best understood as a compiler intermediate representation, not an obsolete format to discard once RDF exists.

rows.source_contract_text:
SKOS is a W3C Recommendation for sharing and linking knowledge organization systems. Its own synopsis already covers most of the required surface: URI-identified concepts, lexical labels, notations, documentation properties, semantic relations, concept schemes, labeled/ordered collections, and mappings between schemes.

Reference:

- https://www.w3.org/TR/skos-reference/
- Notations: https://www.w3.org/TR/skos-reference/#notations
- User-pointed section: https://www.w3.org/TR/skos-reference/#L4307

The compiler should preferentially use these first-class SKOS primitives before defining project-specific vocabulary:

rows.source_contract_text:
Use `skos:Concept` for addressable semantic values.

For grammar values where the corpus already has a stable category/value identity, the obvious initial semantic key is the stable pair:

```text
(category_code, value_code)
```

For example, Configuration `MFF` is one semantic concept even if it later has more than one legal realization.

Do not mint separate semantic concepts merely because a source concept has multiple allomorphs or written forms.

rows.requirement: Concept schemes
rows.reviewer_note: Reviewed SKOS-first contracts, stable IRIs, exact typed notation, shape/label/relation/mapping positive and negative fixtures.
rows.source_contract_text:
Use `skos:ConceptScheme` to separate independently governed semantic inventories where that distinction is real.

Likely schemes include, subject to implementation proof:

- source-grounded New Ithkuil semantics;
- Bilqis-native semantic additions;
- later versioned or independently governed vocabularies that should be mapped rather than collapsed.

A concept may participate in more than one scheme where SKOS semantics permit it and the underlying identity really is shared.

Do not use concept schemes to encode curriculum order.

rows.reviewer_note: Reviewed SKOS-first contracts, stable IRIs, exact typed notation, shape/label/relation/mapping positive and negative fixtures. All 6062 residue rows accounted; 271 affix degrees, 1917 compositions, 3855 components, 19 allomorph rules. 13 source-proven extension properties; ordered composition and rule conditions are not taxonomy.
rows.source_contract_text:
Use `skos:Collection` for grammatical or semantic families where membership is real but subsumption is not.

Use `skos:OrderedCollection` only when the source defines a meaningful order in the paradigm itself.

Examples of likely collection candidates include Configuration, Affiliation, Case families, Aspect, Valence, Phase, Level, Register, etc.

Do **not** turn family membership into `skos:broader` / `skos:narrower` simply because concepts appear together in one grammar table.

Likewise, source-defined linguistic component order may be represented as order when needed, but curriculum teaching order remains a separate concern.

rows.requirement: Lexical labels
rows.reviewer_note: Reviewed SKOS-first contracts, stable IRIs, exact typed notation, shape/label/relation/mapping positive and negative fixtures.
rows.source_contract_text:
Use SKOS lexical labels for human-readable lexicalization:

- `skos:prefLabel` for the canonical human gloss in a language;
- `skos:altLabel` for legitimate alternate labels/synonyms;
- `skos:hiddenLabel` for search aliases, historical spellings, or non-display lexical forms when appropriate.

Respect the SKOS integrity condition that a concept has at most one preferred lexical label per language tag.

Do not abuse labels to carry symbolic notation or structured grammatical metadata.

SKOS-XL should remain optional and be introduced only if labels themselves need first-class identity, metadata, or inter-label relations that core SKOS cannot express.

rows.source_contract_text:
This is a core requirement.

`skos:notation` should carry the literal New Ithkuil notation for roots and other semantic resources borrowed from New Ithkuil.

The SKOS Recommendation defines notation as a typed literal whose lexical form is a Unicode string and whose datatype URI identifies the notation system. It permits multiple notations, including notations from different systems, and deliberately declares no domain restriction on `skos:notation`.

That gives us exactly the mechanism needed for actual Ithkuil UTF-8 forms without creating a project-specific "realization object" merely to store the notation.

Example shape:

```turtle
bilqis:someConcept
    a skos:Concept ;
    skos:notation "ACTUAL-ITHKUIL-FORM"^^bilqis:NewIthkuilNotation ;
    skos:prefLabel "canonical English gloss"@en ;
    skos:inScheme bilqis:NewIthkuil .
```

Where the same resource has another genuine notation system, multiple typed notations may coexist:

```turtle
bilqis:someConcept
    skos:notation "..."^^bilqis:NewIthkuilNotation ;
    skos:notation "..."^^bilqis:BilqisPasigraphy .
```

Grammar abbreviations/codes such as `MFF`, `DPX`, etc. may likewise be represented as a separate notation system if useful:

```turtle
bilqis:MFF
    skos:notation "MFF"^^bilqis:IthkuilGrammarCode ;
    skos:notation "ẓ"^^bilqis:NewIthkuilNotation .
```

The datatype URI should identify/document the notation system. Do not give a typed notation literal a language tag.

By SKOS convention, notation should identify concepts unambiguously within a scheme. The compiler must detect and report same-scheme notation collisions rather than silently accepting ambiguous identifiers.

rows.source_contract_text:
Use SKOS semantic relations when their semantics actually fit:

- `skos:broader`
- `skos:narrower`
- `skos:related`

Do not force every Ithkuil relation into these three predicates.

A grammatical family is not automatically a hierarchy.

An allomorph relation is not automatically `skos:related`.

A composition edge is not automatically broader/narrower.

Where a recurring typed relationship genuinely specializes a SKOS semantic relationship, define the narrowest necessary RDF property, potentially as a subproperty of the appropriate SKOS relation. Where it does not, keep it as a separate linguistic/source relation rather than lying to SKOS.

The project-specific vocabulary should be the **residue after SKOS**, not the starting point.

rows.source_contract_text:
Do not flatten lexical form and semantic sense into one object merely because a CSV row contains both.

The current lexicon source tables distinguish roots and root senses. A New Ithkuil root may support multiple Stem x Specification meanings.

The compiler must preserve this distinction.

A source root's exact written form should be represented with `skos:notation` wherever that resource is being used as a SKOS-addressable notation-bearing resource.

The semantic senses derived from that root should be independently addressable concepts where the source distinguishes them.

Because SKOS deliberately does not constrain the domain of `skos:notation`, we do not need to falsely assert that a root-form resource is itself one indivisible semantic concept merely to give it a notation.

The implementation should prove a deterministic root/sense shape against the current `lexicon_roots.csv` and `lexicon_root_senses.csv` without:

- collapsing multiple senses into one concept;
- duplicating one semantic sense simply because it has multiple surface forms;
- losing Stem or Specification distinctions;
- making source order into curriculum order.

If a minimal Bilqis relation is needed to connect a notation-bearing root resource to its source-grounded sense concepts, add only that relation rather than designing a parallel lexical ontology preemptively.

OntoLex or another lexical ontology can be evaluated later if concrete requirements exceed SKOS plus a very small Bilqis extension. It is not a prerequisite to this compiler.

rows.source_contract_text:
SKOS is **not** being adopted as Bilqis's provenance, attribution, attestation, evidence, claim-consequence, or epistemic protocol.

Those responsibilities remain separately owned.

The semantic projection may retain source references needed to trace a concept back to the public source corpus, e.g. with existing source IDs and/or standard source-reference properties, but that does not turn SKOS into a provenance or attestation system.

Likewise, Rosetta should not be baked into the SKOS model merely because Rosetta may later consume, cite, compare, map, or reason over it.

The clean separation is:

```text
Bilqis / SKOS semantic corpus
        answers: "what does this mean and how is it organized?"

other evidence/provenance/attestation layers
        answer: "where did this assertion come from, who made it,
                  how strongly is it supported, and what happened to it?"
```

The compiler should be ordinary deterministic code, not a standing LLM interpretation step.

LLMs may help investigate a previously unseen source pattern while developing the compiler. Once a source pattern and semantic rule are understood and accepted, encode the rule as code plus fixtures/tests.

Development loop:

```text
new source shape
    -> investigate semantics
    -> define accepted mapping rule
    -> encode deterministic parser/compiler rule
    -> add fixture/regression test
    -> subsequent runs require no model interpretation
```

For a fixed source/CSV state, repeated compilation must produce byte-stable or canonically equivalent semantic output.

The compiler must fail closed on unresolved ambiguity rather than manufacturing a confident semantic assertion.

rows.source_contract_text:
Once the deterministic source and semantic compiler steps are stable, package the workflow as a reusable project Skill so future agents can extend and rebuild the corpus without rediscovering the process.

The Skill should orchestrate deterministic scripts, not replace them with prose instructions or repeated LLM interpretation.

Its high-level workflow should be:

```text
1. resolve and pin source corpus
2. fetch source material
3. extract source structure
4. build morphology
5. build lexicon/root senses
6. build enrichment/crosswalks where applicable
7. validate relational source graph
8. compile RDF/SKOS projection
9. validate semantic projection
10. materialize owned Falkor graph when requested
11. read back semantic smoke queries
12. emit coverage/build receipt
```

The reusable workflow must preserve the distinction between:

- source truth;
- relational compiler IR;
- semantic projection;
- graph-store materialization;
- curriculum/admission;
- evidence/provenance/attestation.

A future agent may investigate a missing extraction rule, but accepted rules should be converted into deterministic code and fixtures so the same semantic work is not repeatedly paid for in inference.
